question.text:
\[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} 3x, & 0 < x < 1, \: 0 < y < x \\[5pt] 0,& \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad f_X(x)= \begin{cases} 3x^2, & 0 < x < 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ and the marginal density function $f_X(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ for $0 < x < 1, \: 0 < y < x.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y (y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0 < x < 1, \: 0 < y < x,$ we have \begin{align} f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\,x) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3x}{3x^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{x}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

\[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\,x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\dfrac{1}{x}}, & 0 < x < 1, \: 0 < y < x \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

question.text:
\[ f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} 3e^{-3y}, & 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad f_X(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & 0 \leq x \leq 1\\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the conditional probability density function $f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)$ and the marginal density function $f_X(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: y \geq 0.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_X (x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

From the equation above, it follows that \[ f(x,y) = f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) \cdot f_X (x). \]

Now, for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: y \geq 0,$ we have \begin{align} f(x,y) & = f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) \cdot f_X(x) \\[5pt] & = 3e^{-3y} \cdot 2x\\[5pt] & = 6xe^{-3y}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)$ equals $0.$ As a result, the product will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the joint probability density function is the following: \[ f(x,y) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{6xe^{-3y}}, & 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: y \geq 0\\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ and the marginal density function $f_Y(y)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 1 \leq y \leq 2.$
question.explanation:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y (y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 1 \leq y \leq 2,$ we have \begin{align} f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{9(x^2y^2+1)}{16}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{3(y^2+3)}{16}\right)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3(x^2y^2+1)}{y^2+3}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\dfrac{3(x^2y^2+1)}{y^2+3}}, & 0 \leq x \leq 1, \: 1 \leq y \leq 2 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

example.title: Working With the Definition of a Conditional PDF

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: \[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{xy+1}{3}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have \begin{align} f_Y(y) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{xy+1}{3} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} \int_{0}^{2} (xy+1) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} \left[ \dfrac{x^2y}{2} + x \right] _{x=0}^{x=2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \left[2y +2 -0 \right] \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2(y+1)}{3}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is the following: \[ f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2(y+1)}{3}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq 2\\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y (y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1,$ we have \begin{align} f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{xy+1}{3}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2(y+1)}{3}\right)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{xy+1}{2(y+1)}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{ \dfrac{xy+1}{2(y+1)}}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: \[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{3x}{8}, & \quad 0 \leq x \lt 2, \: x^2 \leq y \leq x+2\\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ for $0 \leq x \lt 2, \: x^2 \leq y \leq x+2.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have \begin{align} f_X(x) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{x^2}^{x+2} \dfrac{3x}{8} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3x}{8} \cdot y \, \Bigg|_{x^2}^{x+2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3x}{8} \cdot (x + 2 - x^2)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3x(-x^2 + x + 2)}{8}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_X(x)$ is the following: \[ f_X(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3x(-x^2 + x + 2)}{8}, & \quad 0 \leq x \lt 2\\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_X (x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0 \leq x \lt 2, \: x^2 \leq y \leq x+2,$ we have \begin{align} f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3x}{8}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{3x(-x^2 + x + 2)}{8}\right)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{-x^2 + x + 2}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\dfrac{1}{-x^2 + x + 2}}, & \quad 0 \leq x \lt 2, \: x^2 \leq y \leq x+2 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: \[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{x+y}}{2}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq \ln{3}, \: 0 \leq y \leq \ln{2} \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ for $0 \leq x \leq \ln{3}, \: 0 \leq y \leq \ln{2}.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have \begin{align} f_X(x) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\ln{2}} \dfrac{e^{x+y}}{2} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{e^x}{2} \int_{0}^{\ln{2}} e^{y} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{e^x}{2} \cdot e^{y} \, \Bigg|_{0}^{\ln{2}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{e^x}{2} \cdot (2 - 1)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{e^x}{2}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_X(x)$ is the following: \[ f_X(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^x}{2}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq \ln{3}\\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_X (x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0 \leq x \leq \ln{3}, \: 0 \leq y \leq \ln{2},$ we have \begin{align} f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{e^{x+y}}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{e^x}{2}\right)}\\[5pt] & = e^{y}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{e^{y}}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq \ln{3}, \: 0 \leq y \leq \ln{2} \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: \[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{21x^2 y}{2}, & \quad -1 \lt x \leq 0, \: x^2 \leq y \leq 1\\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ for $-1 \lt x \leq 0, \: x^2 \leq y \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have \begin{align} f_X(x) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{x^2}^{1} \dfrac{21x^2 y}{2} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{21x^2}{2} \int_{x^2}^{1} y \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{21x^2}{2} \cdot \dfrac{y^2}{2} \, \Bigg|_{x^2}^{1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{21x^2}{4} \cdot (1 - x^4)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{21x^2(1 - x^4)}{4}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_X(x)$ is the following: \[ f_X(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{21x^2(1 - x^4)}{4}, & \quad -1 \lt x \leq 0\\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_X (x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $-1 \lt x \leq 0, \: x^2 \leq y \leq 1,$ we have \begin{align} f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{21x^2 y}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{21x^2(1 - x^4)}{4}\right)}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2y}{1 - x^4}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\dfrac{2y}{1 - x^4}}, & \quad -1 \lt x \leq 0, \: x^2 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function: \[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} 2e^{-2x - y}, & \quad x \geq 0, \: y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ for $ x \geq 0, \: y \geq 0.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have \begin{align} f_Y(y) & = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x,y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\infty} 2e^{-2x - y} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2e^{- y} \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{0}^{b} e^{-2x} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = 2e^{- y} \lim_{b\to\infty} \left(-\dfrac{e^{-2x}}{2}\right)\Bigg|_{0}^{b} \\[5pt] & = e^{- y} \lim_{b\to\infty} \left(1-e^{-2b}\right) \\[5pt] & = e^{-y}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is the following: \[ f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} e^{-y}, & \quad y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}, \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $x \geq 0, \: y \geq 0,$ we have \begin{align} f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) & = \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2e^{-2x - y}}{e^{-y}}\\[5pt] & = 2e^{-2x}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following: \[ f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) = \begin{cases} \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2e^{-2x}}, & \quad x \geq 0, \: y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

topic.name: Conditional Distributions for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

\[ f_{Y \,|\, X}(y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{y}{x^2}& \quad 0 < x \leq 2 , \: 0 \leq y\leq \sqrt{2}\,x \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find $P \left(\dfrac{1}{4} < Y \,\bigg|\, X=\dfrac{3}{2}\right).$
question.explanation:
Recall that

\[ P(Y \in A \,|\,X = x) = \int_A f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) \, \textrm{d}x, \]

where $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$

In our case, we have

\[\begin{align} P \left( \dfrac{1}{4} < Y \,\bigg|\, X=\dfrac{3}{2}\right) &= \int_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2} f_{Y \,|\, X} \left(y \,\Big|\, x=\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \textrm dy\\[5pt] &= \int_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2} \dfrac{y}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2}\, \textrm dy\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{9} \int_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2} y \, \textrm dy\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{9}\left[{\dfrac{y^2}{2}}\right]_{1/4}^{3\sqrt{2}/2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{9}\left(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2- \left( \dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{9}\left(\dfrac{9}{2}-\dfrac{1}{16}\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{9}\cdot \dfrac{71}{16}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{71}{72}. \end{align}\]

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

\[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{3(x+2y)}{2}, & \quad 0\leq y \leq x \leq 1\\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find $P \left( X < \dfrac{2}{5} \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac 15\right).$
question.explanation:
Recall that

\[ P(Y \in A \,|\, X = x) = \int_A f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) \, \textrm{d}y, \]

where $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

\begin{align} f_Y(y) &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{y}^{1} \dfrac{3(x+2y)}{2} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{2} \int_{y}^{1} (x+2y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \frac{3}{2}\left[\dfrac12x^2+ 2xy \right]_{x=y}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + 2y - \dfrac{1}{2}y^2 - 2y^2\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{2}\left[ \dfrac{1+4y-5y^2}{2}\right] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3(1+4y-5y^2)}{4}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is the following:

\[ f_Y(y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{3(1+4y-5y^2)}{4}, & \quad 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x\,|\, y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}. \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y (y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\leq y \leq x \leq 1,$ we have

\begin{align} f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3(x+2y)}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{3(1+4y-5y^2)}{4}\right)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5y^2}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y-5y^2}, & \quad0\leq y \leq x \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Finally, we compute our probability:

\begin{align*} P \left( X < \dfrac{2}{5} \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac 15\right) &= \int_{y}^{2/5} f_{X \,|\, Y} \left(x \,\Big|\, y=\dfrac15\right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{1/5}^{2/5} \dfrac{2\left(x+2\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)\right)}{\left(1+4\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)-5\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)^2\right)}\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &= \int_{1/5}^{2/5} \dfrac{2\left(x+\dfrac{2}{5}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{8}{5}\right)}\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\int_{1/5}^{2/5} (5x+2)\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{5x^2}{2} +2x\right]_{1/5}^{2/5}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}+\dfrac{4}{5}-\dfrac{1}{10}-\dfrac{2}{5} \right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{7}{10}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7}{40}. \end{align*}

topic.name: Conditional Distributions for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y}(x \,|\, y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2x+2y}{2y+1}, & \quad 0< x < 1, \: 0 < y < 1 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find $P \left( X < \dfrac{3}{4} \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac{1}{2}\right).$
question.explanation:
Recall that

\[ P(X \in A \,|\, Y = y) = \int_A f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) \, \textrm{d}x, \]

where $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$

In our case, we have

\[\begin{align} P \left( X < \dfrac34 \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac 12\right) &= \int_{0}^{3/4} f_{X \,|\, Y} \left(x \,\Big|\, y=\dfrac12 \right) \textrm dx\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3/4} \dfrac{\left(2x+2\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{\left(2\cdot \dfrac 12+1\right)}\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{3/4} ( 2x+1) \, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2} \Big[{x^2+ x}\Big]_{0}^{3/4}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\left(\dfrac34\right)^2+\dfrac{3}{4}-0\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac 9{16} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{21}{16}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{21}{32}. \end{align}\]

topic.name: Conditional Distributions for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

\[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} 2xe^y, & \quad 0\leq x \leq 1, 0 \leq y \leq \ln 2 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find $P \left(X< Y \,\bigg|\, X=\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2} \right)\right).$
question.explanation:
Recall that

\[ P(Y \in A \,|\, X = x) = \int_A f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) \, \textrm{d}y, \]

where $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have

\begin{align} f_X(x) &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\ln2} 2xe^{y} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2x\int_{0}^{\ln2} e^{y} \, \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2x\left[ e^{y} \right]_{0}^{\ln{2}} \\[5pt] &= 2x(2-1) \\[5pt] &= 2x. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_X(x)$ is the following:

\[ f_X(x)= \begin{cases} 2x, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_X (x)}. \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_X (x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0< x < 1, 0 < y < \ln 2,$ we have

\begin{align} f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\,x) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_X(x)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2xe^{y}}{2x} \\[5pt] &= e^y. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

\[ f_{Y \,|\, X} (y \,|\, x) = \begin{cases} e^y, & \quad 0\leq y \leq \ln{2}\\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Finally, we compute our probability:

\begin{align*} P \left(X < Y \,\bigg|\, X=\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right) &=P \left(\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2} \right)< Y \,\bigg|\, X=\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right)\\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln(3/2)}^{\ln2} f_{Y \,|\, X} \left(y \,\Big|\, x=\ln\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{\ln(3/2)}^{\ln2} e^y\, \textrm dy\\[5pt] &= \left[e^y\right]_{\ln(3/2)}^{\ln2}\\[5pt] &=2 - \dfrac{3}{2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

topic.name: Conditional Distributions for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

\[ f(x,y)=\begin{cases} \dfrac{x+y}{3}, & \quad 0\leq x \leq 2,\: 0 \leq y \leq 1\\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find $P \left( X < \dfrac{2}{3} \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac 12\right).$
question.explanation:
Recall that

\[ P(Y \in A \,|\, X = x) = \int_A f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) \, \textrm{d}y, \]

where $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

\begin{align} f_Y(y) &= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{x+y}{3} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3} \int_{0}^{2} (x+y) \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2} + xy \right]_{x=0}^{x=2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3}\left(2 + 2y- 0\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(y+1)}{3}. \end{align}

So, the full expression for $f_Y(y)$ is the following:

\[ f_Y(y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{2(y+1)}{3}, & \quad 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x\,|\, y) =\dfrac{f(x, y)}{f_Y (y)}. \]

where

  • $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

  • $f_Y (y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\leq x \leq 2, 0 \leq y \leq 1,$ we have

\begin{align} f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\,y) &= \dfrac{f(x,y)}{f_Y(y)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{x+y}{3}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2(y+1)}{3} \right)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{x+y}{2(y+1)}. \end{align}

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, $f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

\[ f_{X \,|\, Y} (x \,|\, y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x+y}{2(y+1)}, & \quad 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0,& \quad \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Finally, we compute our probability:

\begin{align*} P \left( X < \dfrac{2}{3} \,\bigg|\, Y=\dfrac 12\right) &= \int_{0}^{2/3} f_{X \,|\, Y} \left(x \,\Big|\, y=\dfrac12\right) \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{2/3} \dfrac{\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}+1\right)}\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{6}\int_{0}^{2/3} (2x+1)\, \textrm dx\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{6}\left[x^2+ x\right]_{0}^{2/3}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{6}\left( \dfrac{4}{9} + \dfrac{2}{3} - 0 \right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\dfrac{10}{9}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{27}. \end{align*}
